conventions.convention: Centered scalar variables are integrable with mean zero; centered vectors have integrable mean-zero coordinates. Sub-Gaussian proxy σ² ≥ 0 means E exp(λX) ≤ exp(λ²σ²/2) for every real λ. Vector proxies control every direction with the additional factor ||u||₂² and impose no coordinate independence.
Sub-exponential parameters satisfy ν² ≥ 0 and b > 0; the quadratic MGF bound holds on the closed interval |λ| ≤ 1/b. Proxies need not equal variances.

Hoeffding assumes AC and independent variables bounded almost surely by deterministic finite intervals; V is the sum of squared interval widths. Thresholds are positive, and V = 0 has a separate zero-tail conclusion.
Bernstein uses centered independent variables, a deterministic absolute bound b ≥ 0, and the actual total variance v. The v = 0 case is deterministic.
Sphere nets have centers on the Euclidean unit sphere, dimension d ≥ 1, radius 0 < ε < 1, and covering distances ≤ ε.

Coordinate oscillation bounds hold for every setting of all coordinates, rather than merely almost surely. Product-integral martingale versions and predictable finite endpoints are used on arbitrary measurable target spaces; endpoint width is at most c_i.
Finite sub-Gaussian maxima require no independence. Scalar and vector zero-proxy cases have probability zero at every positive threshold.

load_bearing.statement: A centered scalar has proxy σ² ≥ 0 if E exp(λX) ≤ exp(λ²σ²/2) for every real λ; a centered vector satisfies the analogous all-directions bound with ||u||₂². A centered scalar is sub-exponential with parameters (ν²,b), ν² ≥ 0 and b > 0, if E exp(λX) ≤ exp(λ²ν²/2) whenever |λ| ≤ 1/b.

For m ≥ 1 centered sub-Gaussian variables with common positive proxy σ², without independence, P(max_j |Y_j| ≥ t) ≤ 2m exp(-t²/(2σ²)) for t > 0. For a centered sub-Gaussian vector in dimension d ≥ 1 and 0 < ε < 1, P(||Z||₂ ≥ t) ≤ 2(1+2/ε)^d exp(-(1-ε)²t²/(2σ²)). Both probabilities are zero for proxy zero. Deterministically, ||z||₂ ≤ (1-ε)^(-1) max_{u∈N}|〈u,z〉|.

For n ≥ 1 independent centered square-integrable real variables with |X_i| ≤ b almost surely for finite b ≥ 0 and v = Σ_i Var(X_i), P(|Σ_i X_i| ≥ t) ≤ 2 exp(-t²/[2(v+bt/3)]) for t > 0 and v > 0; the probability is zero when v = 0.

For n ≥ 1 independent centered sub-exponential X_i with parameters (ν_i²,b_i), b_i > 0, set v = Σ_i ν_i² and b = max_i b_i. For t > 0 and v > 0, P(|Σ_i X_i| ≥ t) ≤ 2 exp[-½ min{t²/v,t/b}]; the probability is zero when v = 0.
Let d ≥ 1 be an integer and 0 < ε < 1. There is a finite N ⊆ S^(d-1) such that every u on the sphere has v ∈ N with ||u-v||₂ ≤ ε, and |N| ≤ (1+2/ε)^d.

For independent random elements and a product-measurable product-integrable real f with pointwise coordinate oscillation bounds c_i ≥ 0, its product-integral sequence M_i is integrable and adapted, each difference D_i has zero integral over every event in F_(i-1), and finite F_(i-1)-measurable endpoints A_i ≤ 0 ≤ B_i satisfy A_i ≤ D_i ≤ B_i almost surely and B_i-A_i ≤ c_i almost surely. No choice axiom is used.

Assume AC. For n ≥ 1 independent integrable real X_i with deterministic finite a_i ≤ X_i ≤ b_i almost surely, set V = Σ_i(b_i-a_i)² and S = Σ_i(X_i-E X_i). For t > 0 and V > 0, P(|S| ≥ t) ≤ 2 exp(-2t²/V), and each one-sided tail is at most exp(-2t²/V). For V = 0 the tail probability is zero.

concerns.concern: Proof step 2.2 says to 'choose almost-everywhere bounds within 1/m of each infimum or supremum' and then takes a countable union of their exceptional sets, while the Statement explicitly claims no choice axiom. The missing choice-free justification is short: choose rational upper and lower bounds by the first suitable rational in a fixed enumeration, within 1/m of the finite essential endpoint. This makes the sequence canonical and retains the argument.

seams_checked.note: The page declares this prerequisite. Its current A-page items do not directly cite batch-14 items; their local bounded-variable MGF route supplies concentration separately. No reverse citation or contradictory restatement was found.

The bracketing maximal lemma correctly applies Bernstein to centered bounded iid summands with absolute bound 2b and variance at most σ². Dudley states the same all-real scalar MGF convention and derives its expected finite-maximum estimate locally. No reverse logical use was found.

The page explicitly says concentration is a planned prerequisite but no concentration inequality is used in its lower-bound proofs. Its current A-page items contain no direct batch-14 citation, and batch 14 makes no reverse use.

Gaussian noise and regression risk items retain the all-directions vector proxy convention. Projection risk applies the net theorem in positive rank, handles rank zero separately, and weakens 5^r to 6^r validly. BIC and sparse support bounds retain that vector hypothesis and zero-proxy handling. No reverse logical use was found.

Score maxima impose no coordinate independence. Product lemmas retain the closed restricted-MGF range. Covariance proofs require independence across observations, use the correct sub-exponential sum constants and sphere cardinalities, and separately control sample centering and zero proxy. No reverse logical use was found.

The univariate trimming theorem expressly cites Bernstein proof step 2.1 for its proved one-sided bound. Its inverse threshold √(2σ²a/N)+2ba/(3N) is a valid sufficient threshold, and deterministic comparison clips satisfy the stated absolute-bound and variance hypotheses. Zero variance is separately acknowledged. No reverse logical use was found.
